```{r setup, include=FALSE}
site <- identical(Sys.getenv("IN_PKGDOWN"), "true")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = site,
                      message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(width = 100)
```

With panel data, the effect of a variable that changes over time can come from
differences between people (people who are married compared with people who
are not) or from changes within a person (the same person when married
compared with when not married). A random-effects model mixes the two. The
correlated random effects (Mundlak) specification isolates the within-person
effect: add each time-varying predictor's person mean to a random-effects
model, and the marginal effect of the predictor, holding its person mean
fixed, is then the within-person effect.

The data are those of the [panel models](panel.html) example: depressive
symptoms among adults aged 51 and older in a 30% sample of households from the
Health and Retirement Study, 2010 to 2020. Marital status and age change over
time, so each gets its person mean.

```{r models}
library(suest)
library(marginaleffects)
library(haven)
library(lme4)

hrs <- zap_labels(read_dta("https://tdmize.github.io/data/data/hrs_si_2025.dta"))
hrs <- subset(hrs, year >= 2010 & age >= 51 & (hhidpn %/% 1000) %% 10 < 3)
hrs$depressed <- as.numeric(hrs$cesd >= 4)
vars <- c("depressed", "marstatB", "age", "woman", "race4cat", "collegeB")
hrs <- hrs[complete.cases(hrs[vars]), ]
hrs$mean_marstatB <- ave(hrs$marstatB, hrs$hhidpn)
hrs$mean_age <- ave(hrs$age, hrs$hhidpn)
hrs[c("marstatB", "woman", "race4cat", "collegeB")] <-
  lapply(hrs[c("marstatB", "woman", "race4cat", "collegeB")], factor)

re <- glmer(depressed ~ marstatB + I(age - 65) + woman + race4cat + collegeB +
              (1 | hhidpn), family = binomial, data = hrs, nAGQ = 25,
            control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
cre <- glmer(depressed ~ marstatB + mean_marstatB + I(age - 65) + I(mean_age - 65) +
               woman + race4cat + collegeB + (1 | hhidpn), family = binomial,
             data = hrs, nAGQ = 25, control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
fit <- suest(re, cre, model_names = c("Random effects", "Within-person"))
```

The marginal effect of being married in each model, and the difference:

```{r effects}
married <- avg_comparisons(fit, variables = "marstatB", newdata = hrs)
married
hypotheses(married, hypothesis = difference ~ revpairwise)
```

**Example interpretation:** In the random-effects model, being married is
associated with a 9.6 percentage point reduction in the probability of
depressive symptoms. Examining only within-person variation, the effect of
being married is a 6.6 percentage point reduction. The random-effects
estimate is 3.0 points larger (\(p < .001\)) because it pools both
between- and within-person variation.
